# Vancouver Fixed-Term Lease End: Tenant Issue Snapshot

A landlord asking a tenant to leave at the end of a fixed term is not always enough by itself. The key question is whether the tenancy agreement, any renewal terms, and the notice timing match BC residential tenancy rules.

## Tenant-Focused Checklist for the Notice and Lease Terms

| Check | What to Verify | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| Lease wording | Does the fixed-term agreement say the tenant must move out at the end, or does it convert to month-to-month? | The exact contract language can change the result. |
| Notice timing | Was written notice served on 2025-08-20 for an end date of 2025-09-30? | Timing and form of notice may affect whether it is valid. |
| Notice form | Is it a proper written notice, signed, dated, and clearly stating the reason and move-out date? | Informal messages may not meet legal requirements. |
| Reason for ending | Is the landlord ending the tenancy because the lease ends, or for another reason? | Different reasons can trigger different notice rules. |
| Rent history | Has rent been accepted after the notice date? | Ongoing rent acceptance can matter for how the tenancy is treated. |
| Prior communications | Were there emails, texts, or verbal statements about renewal or moving out? | Earlier promises or contradictions may be relevant. |
| Tenant protections | Is the tenant in a protected situation, such as a dispute about repairs, retaliation, or accommodation issues? | Extra protections may apply depending on the facts. |

## Documents and Records to Gather

- The signed lease and any renewal or addendum pages
- All written notices from the landlord, including the 2025-08-20 notice
- Email, text, or messaging history about the end date or move-out request
- Proof of rent payments and any receipts
- Move-in condition inspection report, if available
- Any letters about repairs, complaints, or disputes
- A timeline of key dates: lease start, notice date, notice contents, and proposed move-out date
- Copies or screenshots of any landlord statements that differ from the written notice

## Calm Response Letter for Clarification

Use a short, polite letter that does not admit anything and does not argue the law. Keep it focused on facts and a request for clarification.

**Draft wording:**

Dear [Landlord Name],

I am writing about your notice regarding the end of my fixed-term tenancy at [address].

I received written notice on 2025-08-20 stating that I should vacate on 2025-09-30. I would appreciate clarification on the basis for this notice and how it relates to the terms of the tenancy agreement.

Please confirm:
- whether you are relying on the fixed-term end date in the lease,
- whether you believe any additional notice requirements apply, and
- whether you are asking for any further steps from me before 2025-09-30.

I want to handle this calmly and in writing. Please also confirm whether you are expecting any final inspection, move-out instructions, or other next steps.

Thank you,
[Tenant Name]
[Contact Information]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Get tenant help] https://tenants.bc.ca/

- BC Residential Tenancy Branch: https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/housing-tenancy/residential-tenancies
- Tenant Resource & Advisory Centre (TRAC): https://tenants.bc.ca/
- BC Residential Tenancy forms: https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/housing-tenancy/residential-tenancies/forms
